subject.title: [Bug]: gateway allowlist mode makes node allowlists unmatchable for host=node execs (precheck resolves bare names against an empty PATH)

question: Should node-host gateway prechecks consume node-authoritative executable identity from system.run.prepare, or should allowlist satisfaction be deferred entirely to node-local enforcement?
rationale: Either approach can remove false prompts, but they assign authorization responsibility differently across the remote execution boundary; unsafe gateway-side basename inference is not acceptable.

options.title: Carry Node Binding
options.body: Return the node-resolved executable identity in the prepared plan, match it at the gateway, and revalidate it on the node before execution.

options.title: Defer To Node Policy
options.body: Treat node-local policy as authoritative for allowlist satisfaction and limit gateway analysis to approval routing and audit controls.

recommendation.title: Carry Node Binding
recommendation.body: Return the node-resolved executable identity in the prepared plan, match it at the gateway, and revalidate it on the node before execution.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent and historical work most strongly connects this person to the affected gateway/node approval and binding contract.
